note: G32: closed-form degree-preserving baseline vs the shuffle null, after reading hyperon-miner's isurp

controls.name: C1_independent_head
controls.must_fire_because: a baseline that reports structure for a randomly placed head makes every excess it has ever scored suspect
controls.can_fail_because: placement is rng.choice over real entities, so degree-correlated placement could produce a spurious excess
controls.null_must_contain: a nonzero excess for a head placed at random over the same entities with matched edge count

controls.name: C2_dependent_head
controls.must_fire_because: a null that explains away a dependence planted by construction cannot exclude chance structure (A20)
controls.can_fail_because: the planted head raises r's degrees on exactly those endpoints, so a degree-preserving baseline could absorb the entire effect -- that is the failure mode under test
controls.null_must_contain: a near-zero excess for a head planted exactly on the body's endpoint pairs

controls.name: C3_closed_form_agreement
controls.must_fire_because: the closed form replaces the sampled null only if it reproduces it
controls.can_fail_because: the closed form treats candidate pairs as independent and ignores the permutation's exchange constraint; if that matters the two diverge here
controls.null_must_contain: a disagreement larger than sampling error
